fill: findings: one per material observation the document makes about a verse (CP-01 to CP-07); lines[].answer: every line answered (captured / already_recorded / not_an_observation)

lines.text: - Psa 118:29 "for he is good": a verb, paired by the rule with "steadfast love". The LORD is the one said to be good.

- **LORD (15) and God (4):** mostly *ṭôb* said of the LORD, for example 1Ch 16:34 and Psa 136:1 "for he is good", and Psa 135:3 "for the Lord is good". This is God's own character (route A, 13.1), not a qualifier of a thing. Not every row is like this. In 1Sa 26:16 ("This thing that you have done is not good. As the Lord lives") the pairing only picked up the next name.

- **"to see" (7):** mostly Gen 1, "And God saw that it was good": God judging his work good, the divine counterpart of bucket 1's "judged good by someone". Ecc 5:18 ("what I have seen to be good") is the Preacher's own judgement, which is a bucket 1 kind of row.
- Pro 15:17 "Better is a dinner of herbs where love is than a fattened ox and hatred with it"
- "understanding" (3): Psa 111:10 "all those who practice it have a good understanding"
- "to seek refuge": Psa 118:8 "It is better to take refuge in the Lord than to trust in man"
- "to hear: obey": 1Sa 15:22 "to obey is better than sacrifice"
- Jer 40:4 "If it seems good to you to come with me to Babylon"
- Mat 3:17 "with whom I am well pleased" (God's own pleasure: route A)

findings.text: 1. How the pairing was done: A pattern is then given by fixed rules, in this order (the first that matches): comparison (better, best, than); judged good by someone (eyes, seems, suits); good set beside evil; doing good or doing well; qualifies the next noun (good X); said of something (X is good); verb (delight, please, be pleasant); noun (delight, pleasure); Spot checks show the patterns hold for most rows, with clear errors at the edges: Psa 118:29 "for he is good": a verb, paired by the rule with "steadfast love". The LORD is the one said to be good.; Est 9:22 "holiday": counted under "doing good".; H2896A in its verb form ("it was good", "it shall be well with") falls under "verb (delight …)", although it is not delighting.

LORD (15) and God (4): mostly *ṭôb* said of the LORD, for example 1Ch 16:34 and Psa 136:1 "for he is good", and Psa 135:3 "for the Lord is good". This is God's own character (route A, 13.1), not a qualifier of a thing. Not every row is like this. In 1Sa 26:16 ("This thing that you have done is not good. As the Lord lives") the pairing only picked up the next name.

"to see" (7): mostly Gen 1, "And God saw that it was good": God judging his work good, the divine counterpart of bucket 1's "judged good by someone". Ecc 5:18 ("what I have seen to be good") is the Preacher's own judgement, which is a bucket 1 kind of row.

2.1 Bucket 3 (269): *ṭôb* said of things, people and acts: These need to come out of bucket 3 before anything is parked. The rule could not separate them because the paired word, LORD or God, carries a T-code.; Examples: Deu 4:21 "the good land"; 2Sa 18:27 "He is a good man"; Pro 15:17 "Better is a dinner of herbs where love is than a fattened ox and hatred with it"; Gen 41:22 "seven ears … full and good"

Caution: an M-code on the paired word does not mean the pair is an inner-being characteristic. Some of these M-tags are loose (#1970): "king" (8, M72), "hand: power" (3), "word" (3). Others are inner characteristics, for example: "kindness" (9): "good kindness"; "understanding" (3): Psa 111:10 "all those who practice it have a good understanding"; "to seek refuge": Psa 118:8 "It is better to take refuge in the Lord than to trust in man"; "to hear: obey": 1Sa 15:22 "to obey is better than sacrifice"; "be poor", "be humiliated", "mourning"; The full list of 117 rows, with the paired word and the text, is in the filter CSV.

2.3 Bucket 1 (254): inner-being candidates: Examples: Jer 40:4 "If it seems good to you to come with me to Babylon"; Est 5:9 "joyful and glad of heart"; Mat 3:17 "with whom I am well pleased" (God's own pleasure: route A)
